note: v1: first version of 'Hail on a Music Box' (Tape Weather t4), GLITCHY IDM-LITE, a broken music box in a lo-fi beat. 86 bpm, 58 bars, 162 s, Dbmaj9 | Cm7(11) | Fm9 | Bbm9. THE CLOCKWORK runs dead straight: a toy piano on a 5-sixteenth cycle, a music box on a 7, Ferrous Bloom's crystal on the quarters, realigning only every 140 sixteenths, all through a wobbling (chorus-as-wow), lightly crushed, occasionally stuttering toy bus. Against it the BEAT is played by hand: a tight kit swung at 0.58, the snare dragged late, kick patterns shifting bar by bar, dropped hats and ghost notes, crushed and taped. THE HIDDEN MELODY is a tape lead that sings wherever the toy and the box coincide (124 meeting points), so the gears write the tune. Form: the toys enter one by one over vinyl crackle, the beat arrives soft, the melody appears, a GLITCH break tears the toy into falling 32nd HAIL, the return lifts the melody an octave, a beatless breakdown, full, and an outro where the gears drop out one by one. Mix: the first render had no floor (35-90 Hz 15-25 dB under the album, master rms -19 / crest 17), so a sine sub doubles the roots an octave down, the bass and kick come up, and the master pushes into its ceiling: 83.0 -> 93.04 (master in range, spectrum 34 -> 69, cohesion 31 -> 66; rhythm 100 from the swing). motifs.md and sounds.md rows added.
next: Spectrum 69: the mids are still 5-12 dB proud (bands 13-24) and the top 7-14 dB shy (the lp 6-7k on the drum and toy buses): open the hats' air, tame the pad/toys' mids; listen to the hidden melody's phrasing; Harry's notes when they come.
